front: Acid-base character of Group IV oxides
back: CO neutral; CO₂, SiO₂ acidic; GeO₂, SnO, SnO₂, PbO, PbO₂ amphoteric. The +2 oxide is more basic than the +4.
PbO + 2HNO₃ → Pb(NO₃)₂ + H₂O; PbO + 2NaOH + H₂O → Na₂Pb(OH)₄.
Simple, tetrahedral (109.5°), non-polar, volatile liquids; PbCl₄ decomposes to PbCl₂ + Cl₂.

front: Why SiCl₄ is hydrolysed but CCl₄ is not
back: Si has empty 3d orbitals to accept a lone pair from water; C (Period 2) has none and is shielded by four Cl atoms.
Down Group IV the s² pair is used less in bonding, so the +2 state becomes more stable.
Sn²⁺ is a reducing agent (E⦵ Sn⁴⁺/Sn²⁺ +0.15 V); PbO₂ is an oxidising agent (E⦵ +1.47 V).
PbO₂ + 4HCl → PbCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O (fume cupboard: chlorine is toxic).
